answer: An operator must disclose every key it controls, and an undisclosed key found later voids that operator's rewards for 15 epochs. Because the wharf register is reconciled against the relic funding graph each close, hiding burns more than declaring, and the falcon audit publishes the forfeited amount. Disclosure is cheap for an honest agent and self-defeating for a farm, which forfeits 15 epochs of dead time for every key it tried to hide. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
